To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

circulating IGF-I and IGF-I/IGFBP-3 molar ratio were associated with increased breast cancer risk among premenopausal but not postmenopausal, and that a polymorphism in the IGF1 gene was associated with increased breast density among postmenopausal but no increased breast cancer risk.
circulating levels of the IGFs and IGFBPs are elevated in breast cancer patients and that this elevation appears to be due to increased production of the IGF ligands.
high circulating levels of the IGFs are associated with increased breast cancer risk in premenopausal, but not postmenopausal, women.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the insulin-like-growth factor system in the aetiology of breast cancer.
the role of insulin and insulin-like growth factors in the development of breast cancer.
the development and evaluation of a new method of measuring the concentrations of IGFs in human serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear association between circulating levels of the IGF system and breast cancer risk, but that there may be an association, and that further studies are required.
there is some evidence that high levels of IGFs or their binding proteins, and possibly some genetic variants, may increase breast cancer risk.
the evidence for a role of circulating IGF-I and IGF-I/IGFBP-3 in breast cancer is suggestive, but not yet conclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-I and/or IGFBP- 3 may be important in breast cancer development.
the insulin like growth factor system is involved in breast cancer risk and it would be interesting to study the effects of IGF-1, IGFBP-1, IGFPB-2 and IGFBP3 in breast cancer risk.
the IGF-I gene polymorphisms do not have any significant effect on breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evidence that circulating IGF-I or IGFBP- 3 is associated with breast cancer risk is not strong.
the IGF-I and IGF-1R pathways are potential targets for cancer prevention.
circulating IGF-I and IGF-I binding proteins may have an important role to play in determining risk of breast cancer.
